<reason>A more convincingly distinguished valuable connectivity from justified public expenditure. It supplied a concrete outcomes-per-dollar test, counted ongoing costs, and acknowledged the harms of waiting. B established plausible benefits and honestly accepted continuing taxpayer support, but did not resolve the opportunity-cost comparison. Its closing mistook agreement on a funding test for demonstration that its recommendation passed. B also repeatedly attributed a permanent-gap concession to A and accused A of refusing a metric before A’s answer was due.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s second rebuttal exposed B’s restriction of alternative-spending comparisons to the same communities despite using a national budget. Its distinction between auctions disciplining bids and justifying the purchase directly undercut B’s claim that procurement safeguards answered the allocation objection. B’s closing did not repair that gap.</best_rebuttal>
